ClientResponses.Response: Hello, we are very sorry to hear about this! To clean your grill grates we would recommend to first do a “burn off” as your Q is preheating. Set your grill on high for about 15 minutes until the temp gets to 500 to 600 degrees or so, and then open it up and brush the grates with a clean stainless steel brush. We have a helpful article on how to keep your Weber Q clean here: https://www.weber.com/US/en/blog/burning-questions/keeping-your-q-in-perfect-shape/weber-30507.html Please let us know if we can assist you with anything else!

Results.ReviewText: These are great portable grills but they’re missing a major major feature… They’re missing the flavorizer bars. That’s the pieces under the grate that the grilling meat drips onto. These are an integral part in creating the fantastic flavor of grilling. Weber’s smaller grills have them, and every other Weber gas grill has them, but the Q Series doesn’t. I’ve had (2) portable and on my 3rd Genesis grill and they have all had flavorizer bars. Results.ReviewText:
Other than using disposable propane cylinders as a fuel source, small portable gas grills are more frequently referred to as “blow-torch cookers” to describe their hot and harsh cooking quality because their portability demands a compact design that leaves inadequate space between the gas burner and cooking grate for the bulky heat-diffusing rack (filled with ceramic briquettes) that gives larger grills a more steady temperature control, a more indirect and even distribution of heat to the cooking grate, and more flavor enriching smoke produced by the meat drippings hitting the hot briquettes.  However, after combining all of the 5-Star areas of a Weber Q-1200 compact grill with a removable *Heat Diffuser of my own design (*perhaps a future aftermarket accessory), its only 3-Star rating (cooking quality) rose to the 5-Star level to make it a truly and totally 5-Star compact/portable grill that’s ready to go toe-to-toe with those huge porch-dinosaurs in the flavor and cooking quality departments.    

MY RATINGS IN A NUTSHELL:

PROS:    All 5-Star Rated
1. Construction Quality  (good materials / quality fabrication as with all Weber products)
2. Size and Portability   (perfect for cooking six patties or small steaks / easy to carry and store)
3. Ease of Use   (very useful fold-out side trays / accurate control of burner’s flame height) 
4. Ease of Cleaning    (two-section enameled cooking grates easy to remove, clean and reinstall)
5. Design  (football-shape promotes circular convection flow to more evenly distribute internal heat) 
6. Replacement Parts Availability   (all components are available and owner replaceable)

CONS:  3-Star Rated
1.  Cooking Quality  (still much better than 1-2 star quality of other compact/portable gas grills)

**Cooking Quality w/ *Heat Diffuser = 5-Stars   (slower/controlled cooking, good smoke, juicy results)
 
Weber engineers did an outstanding job of designing a heavy, cast iron, enameled, 2-section cooking grate that quickly distributes and retains burner heat throughout the grate’s entire area much better than the skinny stainless steel or wire grates that come with most other compact grills.  Other great design features are the solid area in the cooking grates over the burner route to protect the item being cooked from direct exposure to burner flame along with parallel drip rails on the bottom to channel the drip path past both sides of the burner to help protect it from fouling and cogging of its flame orifices.  However, while cooking quality of the Q-1200 is better than my two previous compact grills (each quickly became garage sale items), there is good logic in guessing that direct-heating from the close-proximity burner produces an excessive cooking grate temperature that could easily be 150-200 degrees hotter than what is indicated by the hood thermometer and usually too hot for comfortable and controlled cooking even at low burner levels.  

Whether I pre-heated the grill at the middle or low temperature setting, it would quickly char very black and deep grate marks (that my wife found un-tasty) on hamburger patties just a couple of seconds after tossing them on the grate, and did the same to the other side after quickly flipping them over (leaving large chunks of charred meat stuck to the grate in the process).  As indicated by the included cooking chart, the patties would cook in about 8 minutes, but the exceptionally hot grate temperature required my constant attention and flipping them every few seconds.  Additionally, there wasn’t a lot of smoke produced, and the patties were a bit dry because most of the quickly expelled juices dribbled into the collection pan below.  Obviously, the greatest caveat of a fast cooking time on a very hot surface is the very narrow timeframe that lies between rare, medium and charred – especially with patties or cuts of meat less than 3/4” thick.

Being a retired major-city fire chief, radio communications engineer and lifelong tinker, I wasn’t about to let one minor detail spoil an otherwise perfect 5-Star product without giving it my best tinker-shot for a good resolution.  After measuring burner flame height at different settings and the distance between burner and bottom of cooking grate, I cobbled together a simple but extremely effective “heat diffuser” from a small piece of stainless steel scrap bummed from a nearby metal fabricating company.  The diffuser is quickly installed or removed, is not attached to any part of the grill, does not contact any part of the burner or cooking grates, does not interfere with burner flame or change its perfect two-tone light blue color (but it does make burner flame considerably more stable in gusty wind conditions), does not block or restrict proper air/heat circulation, and does not create any condition that could possibly extinguish burner flame and/or create a dangerous propane buildup if burner flame was extinguished by any other cause.  

What my new Heat Diffuser DOES do is bring the Q-1200’s cooking grate temperature down to a level more relative to large grills equipped with a heat diffuser rack laden with ceramic briquettes to leave only brown (not charred black) grate marks on meat being cooked, produces just as much cooking smoke as large grills by drippings falling onto heat diffuser (which also protects burner from contamination), greatly stabilizes burner flame during gusty wind conditions, makes the cooking grates much easier to clean without charred deposits, and cooks about 25% slower than most cooking times on the cooking chart - which gives more accurate control of rare-to-well done timing that leaves the meat much juicier, with more smoky flavor.  

Since my *Heat Diffuser makes such a radical improvement in cooking quality and is quickly removable (should anyone desire taking a step back to blow-torch cooking), I have initiated the process to obtain a “patent pending” classification because I am sure the huge popularity and high quality of the Q-series grills combined with the vast numbers already sold will instantly create a great sales potential for such a versatile and effective aftermarket accessory that I will soon begin publicizing via other reviews and on social media.  Obviously, I cannot submit pictures of my Heat Diffuser due to pending patent protection; however, only the superior design and construction quality of Weber Q-Series grills make possible such a relatively simple method of greatly improving its cooking quality.
Results.Title: WEBER Q-1200 – MAKING THE BEST EVEN BETTER

ClientResponses.Response:
Hi Allen, thank you for taking your time to submit your feedback! We are very sorry to see the rust damage. Your grill grate should not be experiencing rust issue, this early into use. It seems like you have reached out to our support team and we just replied back to you regarding your grill grate. As for your LP cylinders make sure that you are using LP cylinders with a capacity of either 14.1 oz. or 16.4 oz. equipped with a CGA #600 connection. When changing your Propane cylinder, make sure burner control knob is turned off by pushing it in and turning it clockwise to the off (O) position. While holding carrying handle closest to propane cylinder with one hand, push propane cylinder into
regulator and turn clockwise until tight. You may find it easier to use the thin cylinder tanks instead of the wider ones. Please let us know if we can help you with anything else! Thanks!
ClientResponses.Name: Weber Grills

Results.ReviewText:
I purchased my grill in March 2020 and it is now May 2020; I had it roughly 2 months and grill out 2-3x a month. I gave it 2 stars because it is a simple and stylish grill that was packaged well, but not a good fit if you're cooking for 3 or more in a family/group. The grill area is an oval shape so the main usable grilling area is 12.5" x 15", small.  There are only 3 of us, 1 adult and 2 children, and we can not fit 3 medium sized 8-10oz tenderloins, onions and/or asparagus, and camping potatoes in foil on the grill at the same time, which means something has to cook first then sits cooling while the rest finishes up cooking. Not ideal.

Other issues I came across was the location of the the regulator connection, it is right under the handle grip making it tricky to grip the grill securely to move it.  I also found it very difficult to install the LP cylinder, they do not go on easily; I have to turn the grill upside down to get the perfect angle to install. My biggest disappointment though was the coating on the porcelain-enameled cast iron cooking grates because it is already flaking off on one of the two cooking grates. I soak the cooking grates in warm soapy water just as the Cleaning instruction recommend and used only a wash cloth to remove cooked on remains and air dry. (If your past the warranty new grates are $65-$85 depending on your grill size) 

The small size I can adjust to, but this is a basic table top grill that is over $200, no one should have to struggle with moving their grill; the cylinder or deal with a rusty cooking grate in this short of time.
Results.Title: Ok grill, but please read...

I like the compactness of this perfect grill. I purchased at a local hardware store, when I got home, the lid was cracked. This would have been fine, but I called the company to ask. They offered the stand that is compatible with this BBQ, I was not wanting to spend too much money on this but they offered me a great deal, paid for shipping and within 3 days I had a new lid and a stand. I have used the grill a few times and am satisfied with how easy it is to use and then put away.
Thank you Weber for making this really easy!
